title: Contact With South East Asia
definition: The process of Indianization (Sanskritization) involving the spread of Indian culture, religion (Buddhism/Hinduism), and political systems to Southeast Asia (Suvarnabhumi/Suvarnadvipa) via maritime trade routes during the Early Medieval period.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding India's 'Soft Power' history, maritime trade networks, and the cultural synthesis that shaped the Indian Ocean Rim.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Contact With South East Asia.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Maritime trade history of the Cholas
Geography of the Bay of Bengal
